autoModeDesc: Find a working strategy for each blocked site automatically
dnsProtectionDesc: Resolve names over encrypted DNS (DoH) so blocks and forged replies are bypassed

shareOnlineCount: Count me in the live total
shareOnlineCountDesc: Sends a random number that changes every launch, so the app can show how many copies are running. It is only sent while protection is on, so it travels the same protected path as the rest of your traffic. Turn it off if you would rather your network saw nothing from Shroudly at all.
restartToApply: Changes apply right away; protection restarts for a moment.
routeListedDesc: Only the sites below go through Shroudly; everything else connects directly and uses your provider’s DNS. Choose this if you want the smallest possible footprint.
routeAllDesc: Every site goes through Shroudly and gets its encrypted DNS, so a blocked site works without you having to name it first. Connections that are not blocked are passed straight through untouched, so your speed stays the same.
siteListHint: One domain per line. Subdomains are included automatically (discord.com also covers cdn.discord.com).
siteListAuto: Updated automatically from OONI measurements: {count} sites, list of {date}. Sites blocked somewhere are added, and dropped again once they no longer are.
siteListCustom: This is your own list, so it is not updated automatically.
logSiteListUpdated: Site list updated: {count} sites ({added} added, {removed} removed)
logSiteListRefused: Site list: the downloaded list was refused ({detail})
logSiteListUnreachable: Site list: could not check for a newer list ({detail})
blockedNoticeTitle: {host} would not open with any method
blockedNoticeNoAdvanced: Advanced mode is not available on this system, so there is nothing further to try automatically. The Logs tab has the detail — sending it to us is the fastest way to get this fixed.
restartAppsBody: A program reads the connection settings once, when it opens. {apps} was already running, so it is still using the unprotected connection it started with. Close it completely and open it again.
obBody1: When a site is blocked, your provider usually spots it by the site name in your very first packet, or by answering your DNS lookup with a lie. Shroudly reshapes that packet and looks names up over encrypted DNS, so the site loads normally. Your traffic still goes straight to the site — this is not a VPN and it does not hide who you are.
obBody2: Press Start and Shroudly points your system at itself while it runs. Press Stop and your network settings go back exactly as they were — and they are restored anyway if the app crashes, is force-quit, or the machine loses power. You never have to undo anything by hand.
obBody3: By default every site goes through Shroudly, and a site that is not blocked is passed on untouched — so nothing slows down and a blocked site works even if you have never heard of it. In Settings you can narrow this to a list of sites instead, and add or remove sites in that list whenever you like.
obTitle4: If a site still won’t open
obBody4: Open Settings and use the site test: it tries the site for real and tells you what is blocking it. The Logs tab records what happened for every site, which is exactly what we need if you report a problem. On Windows and Linux there is also Advanced mode for networks that the normal mode cannot get past.
obTitle5: If you need to ask us
obBody5: This tab records what Shroudly did: your system, your network, and for each site the technique that worked or how many were tried before giving up. If something does not work, copy what is here and send it with your report — it usually answers the question on its own, with no back and forth.

appModeDesc: Sends Roblox, its installer and other programs that ignore the system proxy through Shroudly as well. Shroudly turns this on by itself when Roblox is blocked.

conflictBody: It reroutes the same connections as Shroudly, and the two get in each other's way. Quit {tools} completely while you use Shroudly.
cutTitle: {host} connects, then the network cuts it
cutBodyAdvanced: This network follows whole connections, not just how they start. Shroudly is already trying other techniques for this site; Advanced mode works below that level and usually gets through.
cutBodyAdvancedOn: Advanced mode is on and the connection is still torn down after it forms. That can be a technique this network needs that is not matched yet, or the server's own address being blocked — which no technique can change, and then only a VPN gets through. If other blocked sites work, this one is the likely exception.
cutBodyNoAdvanced: Shroudly is already trying other techniques for this site. If it keeps happening, the network is blocking the server's address or needs Advanced mode, which only Windows and Linux have; a VPN is then the remaining option.
dnsDownTitle: Encrypted DNS is blocked on this network
dnsDownBody: Shroudly keeps trying other routes on its own. Until one gets through, some sites may be sent to fake addresses; the fake addresses Shroudly knows are refused.

technique_frag_desc: The first TCP packet of each connection is split into small segments. DPI systems that don't reassemble TCP streams can't read the full Host/SNI field and let the connection through.
technique_disorder_desc: Segments are sent out of order (last one first). The destination's TCP stack puts them back together correctly, but DPI systems that read packets in sequence can't identify the connection.
technique_dns_desc: Names are resolved through several independent public resolvers at once and forged answers are discarded, so DNS-based blocking is defeated without changing your system DNS settings.
technique_http_desc: For plain HTTP connections the "Host:" header is rewritten as "hoSt:". Simple DPI systems that look for the exact text "Host:" no longer find it.
safetyDesc: By default Shroudly needs no driver and no administrator rights: while active it only points your system at a local proxy, and it restores the previous setting when it stops, crashes or you sign out, so your connection is never left broken. Advanced mode runs only when a site needs it or you turn it on, and only after your system asks for permission.
technique_probe_desc: When a site stays blocked, Shroudly tests each bypass strategy against it over a real connection and remembers the one that works, so the next visit uses it right away.
technique_advanced_desc: Against DPI that reassembles connections, Shroudly can send a decoy copy of the first packet that the filter reads but that expires before it reaches the site. Available on Windows and Linux, it needs administrator permission; Shroudly turns it on by itself when a site needs it.
updatesDesc: Shroudly checks GitHub for new versions when it starts and every 30 minutes.
updLaterHint: It will be installed the next time Shroudly quits.
updManual: Shroudly can’t update itself from this location. Move it to the Applications folder, or download the new version.
updError: Couldn’t check for updates. Shroudly will try again later.
updUnsupported: Automatic updates are not available in this build.
openSourceDesc: Shroudly is free and open source under the MIT license: anyone can read, audit and build its code.
autoUpdateDesc: Download new versions in the background and restart Shroudly to install them
appStoreEdition: The Microsoft Store edition of Roblox cannot reach Shroudly. Install the regular edition from roblox.com instead.
quitAppDesc: Stops protection and puts every setting back.
probeServiceBody: The network is no longer in the way: {host} answers, but says it does not serve visitors from where you are. That is the site's own decision, made from your address, which Shroudly never changes, so it cannot change this.
probeStallTitle: {host} accepts the connection, then goes silent
probeStallBody: Either the site turns away visitors from where you are, or this network stops connections to it once they are made. Shroudly cannot tell these two apart; if other blocked sites open, the site itself is the more likely cause.

For Firefox, enter {pac} as the automatic proxy configuration URL in its network settings.

androidLockdownOffline: No internet: Shroudly cannot get through on this network right now, and Android is set to block connections without a VPN. Shroudly keeps trying.
notifyLogsCopied: The log is on the clipboard. Paste it into your message or report.
autoAdvancedOffBefore: {host} needs Advanced mode on this network. It was turned off on {date}, so Shroudly does not turn it on by itself: turn it on in Settings.
autoAdvancedDeclinedBefore: {host} needs Advanced mode on this network. It was not allowed on {date}, so Shroudly does not ask by itself: turn it on in Settings.
autoAdvancedFailedBefore: {host} needs Advanced mode on this network, but it could not be turned on earlier. Try turning it on in Settings.
autoAdvancedAntiCheat: {host} needs Advanced mode on this network, but a game's anti-cheat ({program}) is running, so Shroudly does not start it by itself. Turn it on in Settings when you want it.
autoDiscordOffByHand: Discord is blocked on this network, but Discord app mode was turned off on {date}. To use the Discord app, turn it on in Settings.
autoRobloxOffByHand: Roblox is blocked on this network, but Games and apps mode was turned off on {date}. To use Roblox, turn it on in Settings.
autoStoreAppsOffBefore: {apps} cannot reach Shroudly: Microsoft Store apps was turned off on {date}. To let them through, turn it on in Settings.
autoStoreAppsDeclinedBefore: {apps} cannot reach Shroudly: permission was not given on {date}. To let them through, turn on Microsoft Store apps in Settings.
logWake: The computer woke up or its clock changed; waiting times start afresh
logHeldRestart: {host}: held back while Shroudly restarts; the program will try again
autoDiscordFailed: Discord is blocked on this network, but Discord app mode could not be turned on. Turn it on in Settings to try again.
autoRobloxFailed: Roblox is blocked on this network, but Games and apps mode could not be turned on. Turn it on in Settings to try again.
autoStoreAppsNoAdmin: {apps} cannot reach Shroudly until an administrator allows it: an administrator can turn on Microsoft Store apps in Settings.
notifyLogsCopyFailed: The log could not be put on the clipboard from here. The Logs panel is open: use Copy logs there.
notifyLogsSaved: The whole log is saved as {file} in {folder}. Attach this file to your message or report.
notifyLogsSaveFailed: The log could not be saved. Use Copy logs instead.
autoRawUnreachable: {app} cannot reach its servers: this network blocks their addresses, and Shroudly cannot get around that without a server elsewhere. Use {app}'s own proxy setting or a VPN.
autoRawBlocked: This network stops {app}'s connections, and none of Shroudly's techniques got through. Use {app}'s own proxy setting or a VPN.
logRawUnreachable: {app} cannot reach its servers ({addrs}): the network blocks those addresses themselves; only the app's own proxy setting or a VPN gets around that
logRawBlocked: {app}: the network stops its connections ({addrs}) and no technique got through; only the app's own proxy setting or a VPN gets around that
logRawUnreachableAddr: {addr}: could not be reached (not a web connection)
logRawStillBlockedAddr: {addr}: still blocked after {tries} techniques (not a web connection)
adBlockDesc: Names on a public ad and tracker list get no answer, in every app. The list is fetched through Shroudly and refreshed weekly.
adBlockAllowDesc: If a site breaks, write its domain here, one per line: it and every name under it are never blocked.
logAdblockInUse: Ad blocking: a list of {count} names in use
logAdblockUnusable: Ad blocking: the list could not be used ({why})
logAdblockFetchFailed: Ad blocking: the list could not be fetched ({why}); Shroudly tries again later
logAdblockRejected: Ad blocking: the list fetched is not one to use ({why})
excludedAppsDesc: Their traffic goes straight out, past Shroudly: for example a game that does not need it.
androidStartAtBootDesc: Protection comes on by itself after the phone restarts, once the VPN has been allowed.
androidModeVpnDesc: Every app goes through Shroudly. Android allows one VPN at a time, so another VPN app is disconnected.
androidModeProxyDesc: Shroudly runs as a proxy on 127.0.0.1:{port} (SOCKS5 and HTTP) and leaves the VPN to another app. Only apps set to use it go through Shroudly: the Wi-Fi network's proxy (host 127.0.0.1, port {port}) or an app's own proxy setting.
androidModeNextStart: The new mode is used the next time protection starts.
androidProxyOnlyOn: Proxy only: apps set to use 127.0.0.1:{port} go through Shroudly
autoForgedDnsOn: This network forges DNS answers, so Shroudly turned on Games and apps mode: programs that do not use the system proxy (command-line tools, bots, some games) now go through Shroudly too. Restart any that were already open.
autoForgedDnsOffByHand: This network forges DNS answers, so programs that do not use the system proxy go around Shroudly. Games and apps mode was turned off on {date}: turn it on in Settings for them.
logForgedDnsAppsOn: Autopilot: this network forges DNS answers ({names}); Games and apps mode turned on, so programs that do not use the system proxy go through Shroudly too
logForgedDnsAppsOff: Autopilot: this network forges DNS answers ({names}), so programs that do not use the system proxy go around Shroudly; Games and apps mode was turned off by hand on {date}; turn it on in Settings for them
logForgedDnsAppsFailed: Autopilot: this network forges DNS answers ({names}), but Games and apps mode could not be turned on ({why}); turn it on in Settings to try again
androidRemoteControlDesc: Tasker, MacroDroid and similar apps can turn protection on and off with a broadcast to the package {package}, action {action}.START, .STOP or .TOGGLE. While this is off, no other app can.
androidAutomationTapVpn: An automation app asked to turn protection on, but the VPN has not been allowed yet. Tap to allow it and turn protection on.
androidAutomationTapBattery: An automation app asked to turn protection on, but Android lets other apps start it only when Shroudly's battery use is unrestricted. Tap to turn it on now.
dnsServerOk: Answered in {ms} ms (example.com: {address}). In use now.
dnsServerFails: No answer ({error}). Not in use; check the address, or use it anyway.
dnsServerDesc: Every lookup Shroudly makes goes to this server. If it stops answering, Shroudly's encrypted DNS answers until it is back.
dnsServerStrictDesc: Nothing else is asked, even when it does not answer: lookups then fail until it does. For testing a server, or when no other may see your lookups.
dnsErrorUrl: That address does not fit this kind; type it like {example}.
dnsErrorHost: That is not an IP address or a server name; type it like {example}.
dnsErrorPort: The port must be a number from 1 to 65535.
autoDiscordDroverMoved: Discord could not connect: Discord Drover sent it to a proxy at {addr} that is not running. Shroudly moved Drover's files (version.dll, drover.ini) to {backup} and restarted Discord. To use Drover again, move them back to {folder}.
autoDiscordDroverDead: Discord cannot connect: Discord Drover sends it to a proxy at {addr} that is not running. Close Discord, move version.dll and drover.ini out of {folder} (to the desktop, for example), then open Discord.
autoAppProxyDead: {app} cannot connect: it sends everything to a proxy at {addr} that is not running. Start that proxy program again, or remove the proxy from {app}'s settings.
autoWinhttpDead: Windows' WinHTTP proxy points at {addr}, where nothing is running, so Windows Update, the Microsoft Store and some programs cannot connect. Shroudly can clear it (Windows asks for an administrator).
winhttpDeadTitle: A leftover proxy is blocking Windows connections
androidWifiProxyDead: This network's proxy is set to {addr}, but nothing is running there, so apps that use it (Chrome among them) cannot connect. In Wi-Fi settings, open this network and set Proxy to None.
androidProxyOnlyOffWifi: Proxy only is off. If this network's proxy is set to {addr}, set it back to None in Wi-Fi settings, or apps that use it cannot connect.
logCustomDnsDown: Your DNS server {server} does not answer ({reason}); Shroudly's built-in encrypted DNS answers until it does
logCustomDnsDownStrict: Your DNS server {server} does not answer ({reason}); it is the only one used, so lookups fail until it answers
logAppsDeadProxy: Games and apps: {names} pointed at {addrs}, where nothing is running; Shroudly's is used while the mode is on, and the old one comes back when it goes off
logDroverMoved: Autopilot: Discord Drover sent {app} to {addr}, where nothing is running; its files ({files}) were moved to {backup} and it was restarted
logDroverStuck: Autopilot: Discord Drover ({file}) sends {app} to {addr}, where nothing is running; its files could not be moved ({why})
logAppProxyDead: Autopilot: {app} sends every connection to a proxy at {addr}, where nothing is running; it cannot connect until that proxy runs again or its setting is removed
logWinhttpDead: Windows' WinHTTP proxy points at {addr}, where nothing is running: Windows Update, the Microsoft Store and some programs cannot connect
logWinhttpNotCleared: Windows' WinHTTP proxy could not be cleared (no administrator's permission)
